label: lem2.1
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem2.1} \cite[Lemma 2.3]{Alvarez2003}
    Let $\{a_n\}_n$, $\{b_n\}_n$ and $\{\theta_n\}_n$ be sequences in $[0,+\infty)$ such that for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$, we have
    $$              
        a_{n+1}\le a_n+\theta_n (a_n-a_{n-1})+b_n, ~\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} b_n< +\infty
    $$            
    and there exists $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ with $0\le \theta_n \le \theta<1$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$.
                            
                    
                                                                                                 
                     
     Then there exists $\bar a\in [0,+\infty)$ such that $a_n\to \bar a$.

label: re1
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{re1}
Even though the functions $\phi$, $g$ and $h$ are assumed only convex, one can consider them, without loss of generality, in the following investigations to be strongly convex, more precisely, $\phi$ and $g$ can be taken $\rho$-strongly convex, and $h$ $2\rho$-strongly convex, for a fixed $\rho>0$. For computational reasons, we will take $\rho>L/2$. Then
$$\phi(x)+g(x)-h(x) = \left(\phi(x) + \frac{\rho}{2} \|x\|^2\right)+\left(g(x) + \frac{\rho}{2} \|x\|^2\right)-\left(h(x) + \rho \|x\|^2\right)\ \forall x\in \mathcal{H}.$$
Note also that, when $\phi$ and $g$ are $\rho$-strongly convex (without the trick mentioned above) and $\rho>L/2$, the set $\Omega_{GDPC}$ contains exactly one element, see \cite[Proposition 3.1]{HDO}. However, this conclusion does not necessarily hold when strong convexity is added to $\phi$ and $g$ are described above.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $\{x_n\}_n$, $\{u_n\}_n$, $\{y_n\}_n$ and $\{z_n\}_n$ be sequences generated by Algorithm \ref{P4Al4.11}.
                                                                                                                           
 When $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\kappa_n(2-\kappa_n)< +\infty$, if $\{x_n\}_n$ verifies $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2 < +\infty$, then it and $\{u_n\}_n$ converge weakly to the same point in $\Gamma_\beta$. Moreover, the sequences $\{y_n\}_n$ and $\{z_n\}_n$ converge strongly to the same stationary point of \eqref{1.1}.

label: e66
title: Proof
body_md:
Using the definition of Algorithm \ref{P4Al4.11}, for a $w\in \Omega_{GDCP}$ and a $y\in \Gamma_\beta (w)$, one has, for a fixed $n\ge 1$,

    \begin{align}\label{e66}
        \|x_{n+1}-y\|^2&=\|u_n+\kappa_n(z_n-y_n)-y\|^2\notag\\
        &=\left\|(1-\frac{\kappa_n}{2})(u_n-y)+\frac{\kappa_n}{2}(2z_n-2y_n+u_n-y)\right\|^2\notag \\
        &=\left(1-\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\right)\|u_n-y\|^2+\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\|2z_n-2y_n+u_n-y\|^2\notag\\
        &~~-\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\left(1-\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\right)\|2z_n-2y_n\|^2\notag \\
        & = \left(1-\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\right)\|u_n-y\|^2+\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\|2z_n-2y_n+u_n-y\|^2-\kappa_n\left(2-\kappa_n\right)\|z_n-y_n\|^2.
    \end{align}
    Since $g$ is $\rho$-strongly convex, from \eqref{eq3.10} and \eqref{eq2}  we have (via Lemma \ref{lem3.1})
    \[
   \rho\|z_n-w\|^2 \le \left\langle z_n-w,\sigma_1 - \sigma_2  \right\rangle ~\forall \sigma_1 \in \partial g(z_n),  \sigma_2  \in \partial g(w)
    \]
    followed by
  \begin{align}\label{eq3.7}
        \rho\|z_n-w\|^2 &\le \left\langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w)+\frac{1}{\beta}(2y_n-u_n-z_n)-\frac{1}{\beta}(w-y)\right\rangle,
    \end{align}
    which implies that (via \eqref{id1})
    \begin{align*}
        2\beta\rho\|z_n-w\|^2&\le 2\beta\langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w)\rangle+2\langle z_n-w, 2y_n-z_n-u_n +y-w\rangle \\
        &\le 2\beta L\|z_n-w\|\|y_n-w\|+ 2\langle z_n-w, 2y_n-z_n-u_n +y-w\rangle \\
        & \le \beta L \|z_n-w\|^2+\beta L\|y_n-w\|^2\\
        &~~+\|z_n-w\|^2+ \|2y_n-z_n-u_n+y-w\|^2-\|2z_n-2y_n+u_n-y\|^2,
    \end{align*}
    i.e.,
                   
      $$  \|2z_n-2y_n+u_n-y\|^2\le -2\beta\rho\|z_n-w\|^2+\beta L\|z_n-w\|^2$$ $$+\|z_n-w\|^2+\beta L\|y_n-w\|^2
        +\|2y_n-z_n-u_n+y-w\|^2         
 $$                
        \begin{equation}\label{e65}
        =(1+\beta L -2\beta \rho)\|z_n-w\|^2+\beta L\|y_n-w\|^2+\|2y_n-z_n-u_n+y-w\|^2.
        \end{equation}

    Now, using \eqref{e13},
    {\allowdisplaybreaks\begin{align}\label{e67}
        \|2y_n-z_n-u_n+y-w\|^2&= \|(y_n-z_n)+(y_n-w)-(u_n-y)\|^2\notag\\
        &=\|y_n-z_n\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2+2\langle y_n-w, y_n-z_n\rangle\notag\\
        &~~-2\langle y_n-w, u_n-y\rangle-2\langle y_n-z_n, u_n-y\rangle\notag\\
        &= \|y_n-z_n\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2+\|z_n-y_n\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2\notag\\
        &~~-\|z_n-w\|^2-2\langle y_n-w, u_n-y\rangle -2\langle y_n-z_n, u_n-y\rangle\notag\\
        &\le 2\|y_n-z_n\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2-\|z_n-w\|^2-2\beta \rho\|y_n-w\|^2\notag\\
        &~~-2\langle y_n-z_n, u_n-y\rangle\notag\\
                                                                            
                                                                               
        &\leq 2\|y_n-z_n\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2-\|z_n-w\|^2\notag\\
        &~~-(2+4\beta\rho)\|y_n-w\|^2-2\langle y_n-z_n, u_n-y\rangle.
        \end{align}}
Since $g$ is $\rho$-strongly convex, from \eqref{eq3.7}, we deduce
\begin{align*}
    2\langle z_n-w, u_n-y\rangle & \le 2\beta \langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w)\rangle+2\langle z_n-w, 2y_n-z_n-w\rangle-2\beta\rho \|z_n-w\|^2,
\end{align*}
    which implies that,
    \begin{align}\label{e68}
        2\langle z_n-w, u_n-y\rangle & \le 2\beta \langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w)\rangle+2\langle z_n-w, y_n-z_n\rangle\notag\\
        &~~+2\langle z_n-w, y_n-w\rangle-2\beta\rho \|z_n-w\|^2\notag\\
        &\le \beta L \|z_n-w\|^2+\beta L \|y_n-w\|^2+2\langle z_n-w, y_n-z_n\rangle\notag\\
        &~~+2\langle z_n-w, y_n-w\rangle-2\beta\rho \|z_n-w\|^2\notag\\
        &=\beta (L-2 \rho) \|z_n-w\|^2+\beta L\|y_n-w\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2-\|z_n-w\|^2\notag\\
        &~~-\|y_n-z_n\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2+\|z_n-w\|^2-\|z_n-y_n\|^2\notag\\
        &= \beta( L-2\rho)\|z_n-w\|^2+(2+\beta L)\|y_n-w\|^2-2\|y_n-z_n\|^2.
    \end{align}
    So, we deduce from \eqref{e66}, \eqref{e67}, \eqref{e68} and \eqref{e65} that
\begin{align} &\|x_{n+1}-y\|^2 \le \left(1-\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\right)\|u_n-y\|^2-\kappa_n(2-\kappa_n)\|z_n-y_n\|^2\nonumber\\                             
           &~~~+\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\left\{ (1+\beta L-2\beta \rho)\|z_n-w\|^2+\beta L\|y_n-w\|^2+2\|y_n-z_n\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2\right.\nonumber\\
        &~~~\left. -\|z_n-w\|^2-2\beta\rho \|y_n-w\|^2-(2+2\beta \rho)\|y_n-w\|^2+(\beta L-2\beta \rho)\|z_n-w\|^2 \right.\nonumber\\
        &~~~\left. +(2+\beta L)\|y_n-w\|^2-2\|z_n-y_n\|^2 \right\}\nonumber\\
        &~~= \left(1-\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\right)\|u_n-y\|^2-\kappa_n(2-\kappa_n)\|z_n-y_n\|^2\nonumber\\
        &~~~+\frac{\kappa_n}{2}\left\{ 2( \beta L-2\beta \rho)\|z_n-w\|^2+2(\beta L-2\beta \rho)\|y_n-w\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2\right\}\nonumber\\
                                                                                                                        
        &~~= \|u_n-y\|^2-\kappa_n\beta(2\rho-L)\{\|z_n-w\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2\}-\kappa_n(2-\kappa_n)\|z_n-y_n\|^2\label{15}\\
        &~~=(1+\theta_n)\|x_n-y\|^2-\theta_n\|x_{n-1}-y\|^2+\theta_n(1+\theta_n)\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2\nonumber\\
        &~~~-\kappa_n\beta(2\rho-L)\{\|z_n-w\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2\}-\kappa_n(2-\kappa_n)\|z_n-y_n\|^2\label{eq4}\\
        &~~=\|x_n-y\|^2+\theta_n\{\|x_n-y\|^2-\|x_{n-1}-y\|^2\}+\theta_n(1+\theta_n)\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2\nonumber\\
        &~~~-\kappa_n\beta (2\rho-L)\{\|z_n-w\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2\}-\kappa_n(2-\kappa_n)\|z_n-y_n\|^2\nonumber\\
        &~~\le\|x_n-y\|^2+\theta_n\{\|x_n-y\|^2-\|x_{n-1}-y\|^2\}+\theta_n(1+\theta_n)\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2,\label{eq3}
      \end{align}  
\noindent as $\kappa_n \in (0,2)$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$ and $2\rho >L$. Using Lemma \ref{lem2.1}, the sequence $\{\|x_{n+1}-y\|\}_n$ converges. Similarly, one obtains that $\{\|u_{n}-y\|\}_n$ converges, too.

  Due to the boundedness of the sequence $\{x_{n}\}_n$,                                                    
                             
    there exists a subsequence $\{x_{n_j}\}_j$ of $\{x_n\}_n$                                     
                                
    such that $x_{n_j}\rightharpoonup \bar x$,                                               
    for some $\bar x\in\mathcal{H}$. By taking into account the way $\{u_n\}_n$ is defined, one can derive $u_{n_j}\rightharpoonup \bar x$, too.

Further, taking into account that $\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|\to 0$ (otherwise, the hypothesis $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2 < +\infty$ would be violated), $L<2\rho$ and $\kappa_n\in (0, 2)$, \eqref{eq4} yields the convergence to zero of $\{\| z_n-y_n\|\}_n$, $\{\| z_n-w\|\}_n$ and $\{\| y_n-w\|\}_n$. Hence, $\{y_n\}_n$ and $\{z_n\}_n$ converge strongly toward the same element $w$ of $\Omega_{GDCP}$.

 Also, we have (via \eqref{eq3.10} and \eqref{eq6}) for all $j\in \mathbb{N}$
  $$  \frac{1}{\beta}(u_{n_j}-y_{n_j})\in \partial \phi(y_{n_j})$$
    and
   $$\nabla h(y_{n_j})+\frac{1}{\beta}(2y_{n_j}-u_{n_j}-z_{n_j})\in \partial g (z_{n_j}).$$
Employing \cite[Proposition 16.36]{BAC}, one obtains
     \begin{align*}
        &\frac{1}{\beta}(\bar{x}-w)\in \partial \phi (w)\Rightarrow
        \bar{x}\in w+\beta \partial \phi (w)\\
        & \Rightarrow \bar{x}\in (\operatorname*{Id}+\beta \partial \phi )(w) \Rightarrow w= \operatorname{prox}_{\beta \phi}(\bar{x}),
    \end{align*}
    as well as
    \begin{align*}
      & \nabla h(w)+\frac{1}{\beta}(w-\bar{x})\in \partial g(w)
        \Rightarrow\bar{w}-\bar{x}+\beta \partial h(\bar{w})\in \beta \partial g(\bar{w})\\
        & \Rightarrow 2 w-\bar{x}+\beta \nabla h( w)\in (\operatorname*{Id}+\beta \partial g)(w)
    \Rightarrow w= \operatorname{prox}_{\beta g}(2w-\bar{x}+\beta \nabla h(w)),
   \end{align*}
so $\bar x \in \Gamma_\beta (\bar{w})$. Lemma \ref{lem2.2} yields then that $x_{n}\rightharpoonup \bar x\in \Gamma_\beta (w) \subseteq \Gamma_\beta$, and the same conclusion can be drawn for $\{u_n\}_n$.

label: e20
title: Proof
body_md:
Define
$$ a_\kappa= \underline\kappa(2-\overline\kappa)>0 $$
and
$$ b_\rho= \beta\underline\kappa(2\rho-L)>0. $$

Then from \eqref{15}
\begin{equation}\label{e20}
\|x_{n+1}- y\|^2 \leq \|u_n-y\|^2-b_\rho(\|z_n-w\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2)-a_\kappa\|z_n-y_n\|^2.
\end{equation}
For $n\geq 1$ denote $d_n=x_n-x_{n-1}$ and $e_n=x_n-y$. Then $u_n=x_n+\theta_n d_n$ and $ u_n-y=e_n+\theta_n d_n$, so
$$ \|u_n-y\|^2 = \|e_n\|^2 +2\theta_n\langle e_n,d_n\rangle +\theta_n^2\|d_n\|^2.$$
Using
$$ 2\langle e_n,d_n\rangle \leq \|e_n\|^2+\|d_n\|^2, $$
we then get
\begin{equation}\label{e21}
\|u_n-y\|^2 \leq (1+\theta_n) \|e_n\|^2 + \theta_n(\theta_n+1)\|d_n\|^2,
\end{equation}
so \eqref{e20} yields
\begin{equation}\label{e22}
\|e_{n+1}\|^2 \leq (1+\theta_n)\|e_n\|^2 + \theta_n(\theta_n+1)\|d_n\|^2-b_\rho(\|z_n-w\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2)-a_\kappa\|z_n-y_n\|^2.
\end{equation}
As $ d_n=e_n-e_{n-1}$, we have
$$ \|d_n\|^2 \leq 2\|e_n\|^2+2\|e_{n-1}\|^2,$$
so
$$ \|e_{n+1}\|^2 \leq (1+3\theta_n+2\theta_n^2)\|e_n\|^2 + (2\theta_n+2\theta_n^2)\|e_{n-1}\|^2.$$

Denote $ M_n:=\max\{\|e_n\|^2,\|e_{n-1}\|^2\}$. As $ \theta_n\leq\bar\theta <1$,
we obtain
$$ M_{n+1} \leq \left(1+5\theta_n+4\theta_n^2\right)M_n\leq (1+9\theta_n)M_n,$$
where we took into account $\|e_n\|^2\leq M_{n+1} \leq (1+9\theta_n)M_n$. Then $ M_{n+1} \leq M_1 \prod_{k=1}^n (1+9\theta_k)$.
Using the inequality $1+t\leq e^t$ for all $t\geq 0$, one gets
$$ \prod_{k=1}^{n}(1+9\theta_k) \leq \prod_{k=1}^{n}e^{9\theta_k} = e^{9\sum_{k=1}^{n}\theta_k},$$
so
$$ M_{n+1} \leq M_1 e^{9\sum_{k=1}^{n}\theta_k}.$$
Due to \eqref{e16}, one gets
$$M_{n+1}\leq M_1e^{9\Theta},$$
so
$$ \sup\limits_{n\ge 1} M_n<+\infty.$$
Noting that
$$ M_n=\max\{\|x_n-\bar y\|^2,\|x_{n-1}- y\|^2\}, $$
one obtains then
$$ \sup\limits_{n\ge 1}\|x_n- y\|<+\infty,$$
so, consequently,
$$ \|d_n\| = \|x_n-x_{n-1}\| \leq \|x_n- y\|+\|x_{n-1}- y\|, $$
so
$$ \sup\limits_{n\ge 1} \|d_n\| < +\infty,$$
thus $\{d_n\}_n$ is bounded. Then there exists a $C>0$ such that
$$ (\theta_n+\theta_n^2)\|d_n\|^2 \leq C\theta_n. $$
Therefore,
$$b_\rho \left( \|y_n-\bar x\|^2+ \|z_n-\bar x\|^2 \right) + a_\kappa\|z_n-y_n\|^2 \leq \|e_n\|^2-\|e_{n+1}\|^2+C\theta_n,$$

and summing from $n=1$ to an $N>0$ one gets
$$ b_\rho\sum_{n=1}^N \left( \|y_n-\bar x\|^2+ \|z_n-\bar x\|^2 \right) + a_\kappa\sum_{n=1}^N \|z_n-y_n\|^2 \leq \|e_1\|^2+C\sum_{n=1}^N\theta_n.$$
So, since $\sum_{n\geq 1}\theta_n<+\infty$, \eqref{e22} yields
$$ \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} \|z_n-y_n\|^2 < +\infty. $$

Consider again an $n\geq 1$. As $ x_{n+1}-u_n = \kappa_n(z_n-y_n)$, one has
$$ \|x_{n+1}-u_n\|^2 \leq \overline\kappa^2 \|z_n-y_n\|^2,$$
so
$$ \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} \|x_{n+1}-u_n\|^2<+\infty.$$
But $ x_{n+1}-u_n = d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n$, so
\begin{equation}\label{e23} \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} \|d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n\|^2 < +\infty. \end{equation}
From Young's weighted inequality, one has
$$ \|d_{n+1}\|^2 = \|(d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n)+\theta_n d_n\|^2,$$
so, denoting $ \eta=\frac{2\bar\theta^2}{1-\bar\theta^2}$, one gets
$$ \|d_{n+1}\|^2 \leq (1+\eta) \|d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n\|^2 + \left(1+\frac{1}{\eta}\right) \theta_n^2\|d_n\|^2. $$
Denoting $q= (1/2) (1+\bar\theta^2)$, as $\theta_n\leq\bar\theta$, one gets
$$ \left(1+\frac1\eta\right)\theta_n^2 \leq q<1,$$

\begin{equation}\label{e24} \|d_{n+1}\|^2 \leq (1+\eta) \|d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n\|^2 + q\|d_n\|^2
\end{equation}
Summing in \eqref{e24} from $n=1$ to $N$ gives
$$ (1-q)\sum_{n=1}^N\|d_{n+1}\|^2 \leq (1+\eta) \sum_{n=1}^N \|d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n\|^2 +\|d_1\|^2,$$
so, letting $N\to+\infty$ and using \eqref{e23}, one has
$$ \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\|d_n\|^2 = \sum_{n=1}^{+\infty} \|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2 < +\infty.$$

then $\{x_n\}_n$ and $\{u_n\}_n$ converge weakly to the same point in $\mathcal{Z}$. Moreover, the sequences $\{y_n\}_n$ and $\{z_n\}_n$ converge strongly to the same limit in $\Omega_{PDRDC}$.

label: eqn18
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $n\geq 1$.
From the definition of Algorithm \ref{P4Al4.1}, we have for a $w\in \Omega_{PDRDC}$ and a $y\in \mathcal{Z}(w)$
    \begin{align}
        \|x_{n+1}-y\|^2&=\|u_n+(z_n-y_n)-y\|^2\nonumber\\
        &=\left\| \left(1-\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)(u_n-y)+\frac{1}{\alpha}(\alpha z_n-\alpha y_n+u_n-y)\right\|^2\nonumber\\
        &=\left(1-\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)\|u_n-y\|^2+\frac{1}{\alpha}\|\alpha z_n-\alpha y_n+u_n-y\|^2
        \nonumber\\
       & -\frac{1}{\alpha}\left(1-\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)\|\alpha z_n-\alpha y_n\|^2\label{eqn18}.
    \end{align}
Like in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem3.1}, one has (from the definition of Algorithm \ref{P4Al4.1})
\begin{equation}\label{e3.19}
    u_n-y_n\in \partial \phi(y_n)\end{equation}
    \begin{equation}\label{e3.20}
    \alpha y_n - u_n + \nabla h(y_n) -z_n \in \partial g(z_n).\end{equation}

   As $w\in \Omega_{PDRDC}$ and $y\in \mathcal{Z}(w)$, it holds (via Lemma \ref{L3.3})
\begin{equation}\label{e3.21}
    \left\{ \begin{array}{l}
  y-w \in \partial \phi(w)\\
  \nabla h(w)-y + (\alpha-1)w \in \partial g(w).
                \end{array}\right.
\end{equation}

    Using the $\rho$-strong convexity of $g$, equations \eqref{e3.20} and \eqref{e3.21} and the Lipschitz-continuity of $\nabla h$, we have
    \begin{align*}
        2\rho \|z_n-w\|^2&\le 2\langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w)+\alpha y_n-z_n-u_n-(\alpha-1)w+y\rangle \\
        &=2\langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w) \rangle \\
        &~~+ 2\langle z_n-w,\alpha y_n-\alpha z_n+y-u_n+(\alpha-1)(z_n-w)\rangle \\
        &= 2\langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w) \rangle \\
        &~~+\frac{2}{\alpha}\langle \alpha (z_n-w), \alpha y_n+y-u_n+(1-\alpha)w-z_n\rangle \\
        &= 2\langle z_n-w, \nabla h(y_n)-\nabla h(w) \rangle \\
        &~~+\frac{2}{\alpha}\langle \alpha (z_n-w), \alpha y_n+y-u_n-\alpha w\rangle -\frac{2}{\alpha}\langle \alpha (z_n-w), z_n-w\rangle \\
        &\leq L\|z_n-w\|^2+L\|y_n-w\|^2-\frac{1}{\alpha}\left\{ \|\alpha y_n-\alpha z_n+y-u_n\|^2\right\} \\
        &~~+\frac{1}{\alpha}\left\{ \|\alpha(z_n-w)\|^2+\|\alpha y_n+y-u_n-\alpha w\|^2\right\}-2\|z_n-w\|^2,\\
           \end{align*}
    which implies that
    \begin{align}
        \frac{1}{\alpha}&\|\alpha y_n-\alpha z_n+y-u_n\|^2\nonumber\\
        &\le L\|z_n-w\|^2+L\|y_n-w\|^2 +\alpha \|z_n-w\|^2+\frac{1}{\alpha}\|\alpha y_n-\alpha w+y-u_n\|^2\nonumber\\
        &~~-2\|z_n-w\|^2-2\rho \|z_n-w\|^2\nonumber\\
        &= (\alpha +L -2-2\rho )\|z_n-w\|^2+\frac{1}{\alpha}\|\alpha y_n+y-u_n-\alpha w\|^2+L\|y_n-w\|^2.\label{3.13}
    \end{align}
    Now, also employing Lemma \ref{lem4.2}, one has
    \begin{align}
        \|\alpha y_n+y-u_n-\alpha w\|^2
        &~~=\|\alpha (y_n-w)-(u_n-y)\|^2\nonumber\\
        &~~=\alpha^2\|y_n-w\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2-2\alpha \langle y_n-w, u_n-y\rangle \nonumber\\
        &~~\leq \alpha^2\|y_n-w\|^2+\|u_n-y\|^2-2\alpha (1+\rho)\|y_n-w\|^2.\label{3.14}
    \end{align}

  From \eqref{3.13} and \eqref{3.14}, we have
  \begin{align}
      \frac{1}{\alpha}\|\alpha y_n-\alpha z_n+y-u_n\|^2&\le (\alpha +L -2-2\rho )\|z_n-w\|^2+\alpha\|y_n-w\|^2\nonumber\\
      &~~+\frac{1}{\alpha}\|u_n-y\|^2-2(1+\rho)\|y_n-w\|^2+L\|y_n-w\|^2.\nonumber
  \end{align}
  Now, plugging this value in \eqref{eqn18}, we have
  \begin{align}
      \|x_{n+1}-y\|^2&\le \left(1-\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)\|u_n-y\|^2+(\alpha+L-2-2\rho)\|z_n-w\|^2+\alpha \|y_n-w\|^2\nonumber\\
      &~~+\frac{1}{\alpha}\|u_n-y\|^2-2(1+\rho)\|y_n-w\|^2+L\|y_n-w\|^2-(\alpha-1)\|z_n- y_n\|^2\nonumber\\
      &=\|u_n-y\|^2 +(\alpha+L-2-2\rho)(\|z_n-w\|^2+ \|y_n-w\|^2)\label{21}\\
      &~~-\left(\alpha -1\right)\| z_n- y_n\|^2\nonumber\\
      &\le\|(1+\theta_n)(x_n-y)-\theta_n(x_{n-1}-y)\|^2\nonumber\\
      &~~+(\alpha+L-2-2\rho)(\|z_n-w\|^2+ \|y_n-w\|^2)\nonumber\\
      &= (1+\theta_n)\|x_n-y\|^2-\theta_n\|x_{n-1}-y\|^2+\theta_n(1+\theta_n)\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2\nonumber\\
      &~~+(\alpha+L-2-2\rho)(\|z_n-w\|^2+ \|y_n-w\|^2)\nonumber\\
      &=\|x_n-y\|^2+\theta_n\{\|x_n-y\|^2-\|x_{n-1}-y\|^2\}+\theta_n(1+\theta_n)\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2\nonumber\\
      &~~+(\alpha+L-2-2\rho)(\|z_n-w\|^2+ \|y_n-w\|^2).\label{eq7}\\
     &\leq\|x_n-y\|^2+\theta_n\{\|x_n-y\|^2-\|x_{n-1}-y\|^2\}+\theta_n(1+\theta_n)\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2,\nonumber\\    \end{align}
 as $\alpha <2$ and $2\rho >L$. Using Lemma \ref{lem2.1}, the sequence $\{\|x_{n+1}-y\|\}_n$ converges. Similarly, one obtains that $\{\|u_{n}-y\|\}_n$ converges, too.

Due to the boundedness of the sequence $\{x_{n}\}_n$,   there exists a subsequence $\{x_{n_j}\}_j$ of $\{x_n\}_n$     such that $x_{n_j}\rightharpoonup \bar x$
    for some $\bar x\in\mathcal{H}$. By taking into account the way $\{u_n\}_n$ is defined, one can derive $u_{n_j}\rightharpoonup \bar x$, too.

Further, taking into account that $\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|\to 0$ (otherwise, the hypothesis $\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|^2 < +\infty$ would be violated), $L<2\rho$ and $\alpha <2$, \eqref{eq7} yields the convergence to zero of $\{\| z_n-w\|\}_n$ and $\{\| y_n-w\|\}_n$. Hence, $\{y_n\}_n$ and $\{z_n\}_n$ converge strongly toward the same element $w$ of $\Omega_{PDRDC}$.

Also, we have (via \eqref{e3.19} and \eqref{e3.20}) for all $j\in \mathbb{N}$
  $$  u_{n_j}-y_{n_j}\in \partial \phi(y_{n_j})$$
    and
   $$\nabla h(y_{n_j})+\alpha y_{n_j}-u_{n_j}-z_{n_j}\in \partial g (z_{n_j}).$$
Employing \cite[Proposition 16.36]{BAC}, one obtains
     $\bar{x}-w\in \partial \phi (w)$, which leads to $w= \operatorname{prox}_{\phi}(\bar{x})$ as well as
    $\nabla h(w)+w-\bar{x}\in \partial g(w)$, which yields
     $w= \operatorname{prox}_{ g}(2w-\bar{x}+ \nabla h(w))$,
  so $\bar x \in \mathcal{Z} (w)$. The lemma \ref{lem2.2} then yields $x_{n}\rightharpoonup \bar x\in \mathcal{Z}(w) \subseteq \mathcal{Z}$, and the same conclusion can be drawn for $\{u_n\}_n$.

title: Proof
body_md:
From inequality \eqref{21}, one can find
  \begin{align}\label{eqn4.43}
          \|x_{n+1}-y\|^2 &\leq \|u_n-y\|^2 +(\alpha+L-2-2\rho)(\|z_n-w\|^2+ \|y_n-w\|^2)\\
&~~-\left(\alpha -1\right)\| z_n- y_n\|^2.\nonumber
    \end{align}
    Denoting $$b_{\rho}=(2-\alpha+ 2 \rho-L)$$
    $$\alpha_k=\alpha -1,$$
    we can rewrite \eqref{eqn4.43} as
      \begin{align}\label{eqn4.431}
          \|x_{n+1}-y\|^2 &\leq \|u_n-y\|^2 -b_{\rho}(\|z_n-w\|^2+ \|y_n-w\|^2)-\alpha_k\| z_n- y_n\|^2 \nonumber.
    \end{align}
    For $n\geq 1$, consider $d_n=x_n-x_{n-1}, e_n =x_n -y, u_n =x_n +\theta_n d_n \text{ and } u_n-y=e_n+\theta_n d_n$ so,

 \begin{align}
      \|u_n-y\|^2 &= \|x_n+\theta_n (x_n -x_{n-1})-y)\|^2\nonumber\\
       &= \|e_n +\theta_n d_n\|^2 \nonumber\\
       &=\|e_n\|^2+\theta_n^2 \|d_n\|^2+2\theta_n\langle e_n, d_n\rangle.\nonumber
 \end{align}
  Since, $$2\langle e_n, d_n \rangle \leq \|e_n\|^2 + \|d_n\|^2,$$
  we get,
  \begin{align}
      \|u_n -y\|^2 &\leq \|e_n\|^2 + \theta_n^2 \|d_n\|^2 +\theta_n \|e_n\|^2+\theta_n \|d_n\|^2\nonumber\\
      &= (1+\theta_n)\|e_n\|^2 +\theta_n (1+\theta_n)\|d_n\|^2. \nonumber
  \end{align}
  From \eqref{eqn4.43} we obtain,
  \begin{align}
      \|e_{n+1}\|^2 &\leq (1+\theta_n)\|e_n\|^2 +\theta_n(1+\theta_n)\|d_n\|^2-b_{\rho} (\|z_n-w\|^2+\|y_n-w\|^2)-\alpha_k \|z_n-y_n\|^2. \nonumber
  \end{align}
  Since $d_n=e_n-e_{n-1},$ we have, $$\|d_n\|^2\leq 2\|e_n\|^2+2\|e_{n-1}\|^2$$
  which inforce
  \begin{align}
      \|e_{n+1}\|^2 &\leq (1+\theta_n)\|e_n\|^2 +\theta_n (1+\theta_n)\|d_n\|^2\nonumber\\
      &=(1+\theta_n)\|e_n\|^2+\theta_n (1+\theta_n)\{2\|e_n^2 +2\|e_{n-1}\|^2\}\nonumber\\
      &= (1+\theta_n+2\theta_n+2\theta_n^2)\|e_n\|^2+(2\theta_n +2\theta_n^2)\|e_{n-1}\|^2. \nonumber
  \end{align}
Denote,
      $$M_n=\max\{\|e_n\|^2, \|e_{n-1}\|^2\},$$ we obtain
      $$M_{n+1}\leq (1+5\theta_n+4 \theta_n^2)M_n \leq (1+\theta_n)M_n,$$
where we took into account $$\|e_n\|^2\leq M_{n+1}\leq (1+9\theta_n)M_n.$$
Then, $M_{n+1}\leq M_1 \prod_{k=1}^{n}(1+9\theta_k).$
Using the inequality, $1+t\leq e^t, \forall t\geq 0,$ one gets
$$\prod_{k=1}^{n}(1+9\theta_k)\leq \prod_{k=1}^{n} e^{9 \theta_k}=e^{9\sum_{k=1}^{n}\theta_k}.$$
So, $$M_{n+1}\leq M_1 e^{9\sum_{k=1}^{n}\theta_k},$$
which implies $$M_{n+1} \leq M_1 e^{9\Theta}.$$
So, $$\sup_{n\geq 1}M_n < +\infty.$$
Noting that $$M_n =\max\{\|x_n-y\|^2,\|x_{n-1}-y\|^2\}$$
one obtains then $$\sup_{n \geq 1} \|x_n-y\| < +\infty.$$
So cosequently, $$\|d_n\|=\|x_n -x_{n-1}\|\leq \|x_n-y\|+\|x_{n-1}-y\|$$
one obtains then $$\sup_{n\geq 1}\|x_n-y\|< +\infty.$$
So consequently, $$\|d_n\|=\|x_n-x_{n-1}\|\leq \|x_n-y\|+\|x_{n-1}-y\|$$
so, $$\sup_{n\geq 1}\|d_n\| <+\infty,$$
thus, $\{d_n\}$ is bounded. Then there exists a $C >0$ such that $$(\theta_n+\theta_n^2)\|d_n\|^2 \leq C\theta_n.$$
Therefore, $$b_p(\|y_n-\bar{x}\|^2+\|z_n -\bar{x}\|^2)+\alpha_k \|z_n-y_n\|^2\le \|e_n\|^2-\|e_{n+1}\|^2+C\theta_n,$$
summing from $n=1$ to an $N>0$ one gets,
\begin{equation}\label{eq4.46}
 b_p\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\|y_n-\bar{x}\|^2+\|z_n -\bar{x}\|^2)+ \alpha_k \sum_{n=1}^{N}\|z_n-y_n\|^2\leq \|e_1\|^2+C\sum_{n=1}^{N} \theta_n.
\end{equation}
Since $\sum_{n\geq 1}\theta_n < +\infty,$ so \eqref{eq4.46} yields $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\|z_n-y_n\|^2 <+\infty.$$
Consider again an $n\geq 1.$ As $x_{n+1}-u_n=z_n-y_n,$ one has
$$\|x_{n+1}-u_n\|^2=\|z_n-y_n\|^2$$
so, $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\|x_{n+1}-u_n\|^2 <+\infty.$$
But, $x_{n+1}-u_n=d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n $ so,
\begin{equation}\label{eqn4.48}
 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\|d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n\|^2< +\infty.
\end{equation}
From Young's weighted inequality, one has
$$\|d_{n+1}\|^2=\|(d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n)+\theta_n d_n\|^2$$
so, denoting $\eta= \frac{2\bar{\theta}^2}{1-\bar{\theta}^2},$ one gets
$$\|d_{n+1}\|^2 \leq (1+\eta)\|d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n\|^2+(1+\frac{1}{\eta})\theta_n^2 \|d_n\|^2.$$
Denoting $q=\frac{1}{2}(1+\bar{\theta}^2)$ as $\theta_n \leq \bar{\theta},$ one gets
$$(1+\frac{1}{\eta})\theta_n^2 \leq q <1,$$
\begin{equation}\label{eqn4.47}
    \|d_{n+1}\|^2\leq (1+\eta)\|d_{n+1}-\theta_nd_n\|^2+q\|d_n\|^2.
\end{equation}
Summing in \eqref{eqn4.47} from $n=1$ to $N$ gives
$$(1-q)\sum_{n=1}^{N}\|d_{n+1}\|^2 \leq(1+\eta)\sum_{n=1}^{N}\|d_{n+1}-\theta_n d_n\|^2+\|d_1\|^2.$$
So, letting $N\to +\infty$ and using \eqref{eqn4.48}, one has
$$\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\|d_n\|^2=\sum_{n=1}^{+\infty}\|x_n -x_{n-1}\|^2 < +\infty.$$
